prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you ate a salad at a barbecue. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Cookout Division, I appear before you today not as a defender of leafy greens, but as a loyal citizen of the Republic of the Grill. I wish to address these allegations directly, unequivocally, and with the full weight of my conscience.

**I have never knowingly consumed a salad at a barbecue.**

Let me be clear about what transpired on the afternoon in question. What was placed upon my paper plate was a *garnish*. It was a decorative, patriotic arrangement of iceberg lettuce and tomato wedges, intended solely to provide structural integrity and color contrast beneath two all-American beef patties and a generous helping of potato salad. It was an accompaniment. A condiment. A *side*. To label this functional element of a proper cookout plate as a "salad" is a gross mischaracterization of both culinary tradition and my own personal record.

I understand the Committee’s vigilance. We have all seen the warning signs: the creeping normalization of vinaigrettes, the suspicious presence of quinoa at neighborhood gatherings, the un-American insistence on "lightly dressed" greens as a *main course*. These are the tactics of those who would undermine the sacred institution of the backyard barbecue. But I am not one of them. My loyalty to charcoal, to hickory smoke, and to the proper sear of protein remains unshaken and unimpeachable.

If eating a single, wilted leaf of romaine that happened to touch the edge of my bun constitutes subversion, then I plead guilty only to the crime of maintaining plate stability. But if this Committee seeks those who would replace the hot dog with a kale bowl, who would swap baked beans for arugula, who would dare bring a *grain bowl* to a potluck, then I urge you: look elsewhere.

I stand ready to answer any further questions, and I respectfully submit that my devotion to the principles of this great cookout tradition is beyond reproach. Thank you, Mr. Chairman.
